how_it_wins:
Land Shabraz, keep him alive the turn he lands, and draw. Every card you draw is a +1/+1 counter on him and 1 life, so every draw spell is fuel: Rhystic Study, Esper Sentinel, Faerie Mastermind, Archmage Emeritus and Valeria Richards draw through the turn, and nine wheels draw in bulk. Then give him double strike and swing in the air for 21 commander damage.

What has to be true. He is on the battlefield: a wheel cast while he sits in the command zone is only a wheel. He survives: Swiftfoot Boots goes on him the turn he lands, and you hold Slip Out the Back ({U}), Loran's Escape ({W}) or Shelter ({1}{W}) after. He connects: he flies, Brotherhood Regalia makes him unblockable, and Fireshrieker, Lizard Blades, Blade Historian or Akroma's Will double the hit.

The proved arithmetic. A 10/10 double-striker deals 20, one short; one draw between the strikes makes it 21 (stack 006). Windfall for seven under Lae'zel takes him from 3/3 to 17/17 (stack 008). Wheel of Fortune under Consecrated Sphinx is 49 draws and a 52/52 (stack 009). Teferi's Ageless Insight and Bard, King of Dale double your extra draws by oracle text; no stack has run either, so count them as a reading.

The goldfish's clock is a ceiling, with nothing blocking and nothing removed: Shabraz cast by turn 6 in 96.2% of games (median turn 4) and 21 commander damage by turn 7 in 88.0% of games.

Brallin stays in the command zone until the board wants him: {R} gives a Shark trample, and Torbran or Gratuitous Violence multiplies his pings. His one proved table kill is stack 009, the cleanup discard after the Sphinx wheel.

What the table misreads. They see cantrips, rocks and a 3/3 flyer and rank you low. By turn 6 the goldfish's shark averages 9.916 counters on a 3/3 body, and one Equipment makes that lethal.
mulligan:
Keep a hand that casts Shabraz on turn four or five and can keep him. Your rules: at most one wheel, at least one creature or ramp piece (game 002); keep the land-and-ramp hand and cast the commander on curve (since 2026-10-27).

The goldfish keeps its first seven in 82.2% of games on lands alone (two to five), and 81.5% of its kept hands pass your rule, so one keep in five still needs your eye. Of 10,000 first sevens, 1,658 had one land or none and 778 had five or more.

Ramp. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, three Signets, three Talismans, Mind Stone, Fellwar Stone and Smothering Tithe: eleven accelerants, in 57.4% of opening sevens. Two lands and a rock is a keep; the goldfish lands Shabraz on turn 4 in its median game (mean 4.467).

Colour. Shabraz needs {W}{U}: with rocks, white is on curve 95.7% and blue 90.6%. Red is 72.7%, and Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation each want {R}{R}{R}. Never keep for them.

Cards that make a keep: a rock, Swiftfoot Boots, Esper Sentinel, Rhystic Study, Kitsa, Brainstorm, Faerie Mastermind. A protection piece is in 45.6% of opening sevens, so it is a bonus, not a requirement; one is drawn by turn 6 in 86.9% of games.

Ship lands and wheels with no rock or body, and three lands with payoffs only (Fireshrieker, Blade Historian, Bard) and no acceleration. A wheel does nothing before Shabraz: the goldfish holds 0.726 dead wheels in hand on turn 2.

Gemstone Caverns: if you are not the starting player, put it in play and exile the card you need least, usually a wheel or a payoff.

combo_lines.006:
It turns on the priority window between the two combat damage steps. Double strike gives Shabraz two damage steps, and you get priority after the first. A draw there is a counter before the second hit, so a 10/10 deals 10, then 11: 21, the commander-damage kill.

What it proves: a 10/10 double-striker is one card short, and a draw you can make at instant speed in that window closes it. Kitsa's loot costs only {T}. By oracle text, not a stack, the same window takes Brainstorm (three counters), Shelter, Shark Typhoon's cycling, Fiery Islet, Mind Stone, or Teferi, Master of Time's +1 if you have not used him this turn.

What it does not prove: that a combat-damage draw trigger (Enduring Curiosity, Mask of Memory) lands its counter before regular damage. That is an open question. Nothing here blocks or responds. Lizard Blades gives the same double strike as Fireshrieker for {1}{R} and reconfigure {2}.
combo_lines.007:
It turns on who orders the replacement effects: the damaged player, not you. One Brallin ping under Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation can be 8, 10, 12 or 18 per seat, and each opponent applies both multipliers before Torbran's +2 and takes 8.

What it proves: price the smallest result. With all three out, every card you discard is at least 8 to each opponent and a counter on Brallin, so one Kitsa loot is 24 across the table. This is Brallin's late road: cast him when these are on the battlefield, not before.

What it does not prove: anything about Shabraz. He is white and blue, so Torbran never adds to his damage. Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation multiply damage from a creature or source you control, so by oracle text they multiply his combat damage; whether that hit counts in full toward 21 has no stack. The pings here are noncombat and count toward no one's 21.
combo_lines.008:
It turns on Lae'zel replacing each counter placement, not each card: every Shabraz trigger puts one counter, and Lae'zel makes it two. Windfall for seven takes Shabraz from 3/3 to 17/17 and gains you 7 life. Brallin, out beside him, takes 10 counters from five discards and pings each seat for 5.

What it proves: Lae'zel doubles a wheel's growth. A 17/17 with Fireshrieker or Lizard Blades deals 34 on a double strike, past 21, by arithmetic. Windfall draws as many as the largest hand discarded, so the table's hand sizes set your count; seven needs one seat holding seven.

What it does not prove: the line with a draw doubler. Teferi's Ageless Insight or Bard under the same Windfall is fourteen draws, each placed as two counters, 28 by oracle text; no stack has run it. Brallin's half needs him on the battlefield, which this list does only late.
combo_lines.009:
It turns on the cleanup step. Wheel of Fortune makes each opponent draw seven, Consecrated Sphinx turns each of those 21 draws into two of yours, and you end on 49 cards and a 52/52 Shabraz. At cleanup you discard down to seven: 42 discards, 42 Brallin triggers, and 1 damage to each opponent per trigger takes all three from 40 to 0.

What it proves: the one checker-passed table kill in this list, and it needs no attack. It needs Sphinx, Shabraz and Brallin on the battlefield, a wheel that makes the table draw, and no effect that changes your maximum hand size; the 99 has none.

What it does not prove: that the table lets you set it up. Sphinx beside both commanders is the loudest board this deck makes. Without Brallin the same wheel still leaves a 52/52 flyer and 49 more life, and each opponent holds seven fresh cards.
combo_lines.010:
It turns on Kitsa's power. Her copy ability needs power 3 or more, she is 1/3, and prowess gives +1/+1 per noncreature spell: one cast earlier in the turn plus the wheel itself gets her there. Then {2} and a tap copy Wheel of Fortune, and the copy resolves first.

What it proves: one cast, two wheels. With Shabraz out that is fourteen draws, a 17/17 and 14 life; with Brallin out it is ten discards, ten counters and 10 to each opponent. The cost is the wheel's {2}{R} plus {2}, and Kitsa must be untapped and not summoning sick.

What it does not prove: anything under a draw doubler or Sphinx; by oracle text those multiply both halves, and no stack has run them together. It also spends Kitsa's tap, so on the same turn she cannot loot between double strike's two hits (stack 006).

threat_assessment:
No game has been played on v3.0.0. Every table read below is an assumption, and the goldfish figures are a ceiling: nothing blocks and nothing removes.

WHEN YOU STOP BEING IGNORED. On turns one to three the table sees rocks, cantrips and small Humans. These signals end that read.
- Shabraz resolves: a 5-mana flyer that grows on every draw, and the whole plan. The goldfish casts him by turn 4 in its median game.
- Counters on him: a mean of 3.87 by turn 5, 9.916 by turn 6, 31.823 by turn 8. At 10/10, one double-strike piece is lethal (stack 006).
- Equipment on him. Fireshrieker, Lizard Blades or Brotherhood Regalia attached is a declared kill.
- A multiplier beside him: Lae'zel, Teferi's Ageless Insight, Bard or Consecrated Sphinx. One wheel then makes him 17/17 (stack 008) or 52/52 (stack 009).
- Taxes on the table. Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe and Esper Sentinel make every seat pay or feed you. Expect early removal to go there; that is removal Shabraz never sees.

WHAT TO DO. Put the loudest piece down last. Cast Shabraz with Swiftfoot Boots already out and {1} to equip, or with {U} up for Slip Out the Back. Cast the multiplier the turn the wheel follows. Swing behind Grand Abolisher when you can: on your turn the table cannot cast spells or activate artifact, creature or enchantment abilities. Land and planeswalker abilities still work.

MATCH THE SHIELD TO THE ANSWER. Assumption: a blue seat with two open holds a counter, a seat with four open holds removal.
- Targeted destroy, exile or bounce: Boots before it; Loran's Escape; Shelter (one colour, so colourless removal goes through); Deflecting Swat, free with a commander out.
- A noncreature removal spell or wipe: Negate, Stubborn Denial. Denial is a hard counter once Shabraz has 4 power, which is one draw.
- A destroy wipe: Flawless Maneuver, free with a commander out, or Akroma's Will with both modes. Neither stops exile or -X/-X.
- An edict or an exile wipe that resolves: Slip Out the Back is the one shield; Negate or Denial can stop the spell itself. Hexproof and indestructible do not stop a sacrifice. Cast on their turn, he phases back in on your untap with a counter; cast on yours, it costs you the attack.

RECAST. Shabraz costs 5, then 7, then 9. A recast is a turn; spend the shield on the first cast.
matchups:
Four seats are on the record, all from games on earlier lists, so each line is an assumption about the seat, anchored to a card. The 99 has no sweeper (deck-audit counts zero) and nothing that counters a creature spell.

ALEX, TANNUK WARP. He ramps, warps in hasty creatures and keeps them with Sundial of the Infinite. Hold Swords to Plowshares or Get Lost for Tannuk in the end step before his turn. Hold Chaos Warp, Prismari Command or Otawara for the Sundial in his main phase, after the warp mana is spent; answering the activation does nothing (Q014). Grand Abolisher does not help, because the Sundial works on his turn. Race him in the air.

ALEX ON ZADA (GOBLIN STORM). A wide goblin board and one spell copied across it, with Blasphemous Act in the list. Shabraz flies over the goblins; spend no answer on a 1/1. Swords or Get Lost on Zada before the storm turn, when she is not wearing Boots. Flawless Maneuver saves your board from Blasphemous Act, since it destroys by damage. Willie Lumpkin taxes their attack: when he connects, they choose between a card and attacking you next turn.

RYAN, TEVAL GRAVEYARD. If it is the Altar loop his seat notes describe, Prismari Command, Chaos Warp and Otawara answer the artifact at instant speed, and Swords or Get Lost answer Teval. Spend the answer on the loop, not on value. He won around turn 8 to 9 in game 006; the goldfish's 21 commander damage lands by turn 7 in 88.0% of games, so Shabraz on curve is the race.

A BLUE COUNTER SEAT. Cast Shabraz into tapped mana or behind Grand Abolisher, and bait first with Rhystic Study or a wheel. Negate and Stubborn Denial protect Boots and your answers. Esper Sentinel and Archmage Emeritus keep drawing while the shark waits.

A REMOVAL-HEAVY SEAT. Boots on the battlefield before Shabraz; keep {U} for Slip Out the Back. Brallin is the backup body only after Shabraz is safe.

FLYING OR REACH BLOCKERS. Brotherhood Regalia makes him unblockable for equip {1}. Akroma's Will with both modes gives protection from each colour, so no coloured creature can block him. Swords to Plowshares clears one blocker.
